The `todo.py` file currently contains a single function, `complete_todo`, which takes a `todo_list` as input. It checks if the input is a list and raises a `TypeError` if it is not. If the input is a list, it appends the string `"Done"` to the list. 

This function does not store any state on its own; it modifies the input list in place. The list itself is the data structure that holds the state of the todo items. Since the list is passed by reference, any changes made to it within the function will be reflected outside the function as well.
